deities: Lord Shiva (Shivlingam; the dol was initially a Devi temple)

history.period: 1750 (documented Ahom construction; one travel site speculates 8th-9th c. Chutia origins - conflict, unverified)
history.summary: A historical doul at Lejai Miripathar village, Larua Mouza, Barbarua Revenue Circle, about 22 km from Dibrugarh town. Built in 1750 by Ahom king Swargadeo Pramatta Singha in the Nilachal architectural style (bricks with indigenous cement). It was initially a Devi temple; over time Shiva became the principal worship, hence 'Shiv Doul' / 'Raidongia Shiv Doul'. Recognised as a State Protected Monument by the Archaeological Department of the Government of Assam. The dol is about 45 feet high; 24 statues once adorned its walls, 14 remain; a large pond stands adjacent. Local legend says the dol, the pond and 200 pura of land were given as dowry when the king married his sister to Raidongia Barua. The historic Raidongia Road linked the site to Gargaon, the old Ahom capital. Conflict: travelsetu speculates an 8th-9th century Chutia origin - not supported by monument records; documented construction is 1750.

name: Raidongia Dol (Shiva Dol)
town: Lejai-Kalakhowa area (CSV town 'Dibrugarh' is approximate - the dol is ~22 km from Dibrugarh town)
town_description: Dibrugarh, the 'Tea City of India', is the largest city of Upper Assam on the banks of the Brahmaputra, about 440 km east of Guwahati. It is a major centre of the tea, oil and gas industries and a gateway to sights such as the Bogibeel bridge, Jokai Botanical Garden and the Ahom-era monuments of the district.

travel.road: Via Raidongia Road off the Lejai-Kalakhowa road; reachable by hired taxi or local bus from Dibrugarh.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (verify); Maha Shivratri (February-March) draws the largest crowds.
